articles.title: 'Nobody can touch it': Trump moves to bar future presidents from changing Oval Office
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump has moved to protect his revamped Oval Office from future alterations, signing an executive order declaring it a national
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has moved to protect his revamped Oval Office from future alterations, signing an executive order declaring it a national monument and placing it under the management of the National Park Service.Trump, who has extensively remodelled the office since returning to the White House, said the move would prevent future presidents from dismantling or making major changes to the space."So we're making it a national monument, and it will not be allowed to be touched by anybody, destroyed, ripped down by stupid people, in order to build something in a slightly different shape," Trump said on Thursday.The order designates the Oval Office, along with some adjoining rooms, as a national monument and directs the National Park Service to protect its historic character and architectural integrity, BBC reported.However, it does not prevent the president from redecorating the office, changing its furnishings or making routine operational and security-related modifications, provided these do not substantially affect its historic structure or architectural character."We like the Oval Office, and it's a symbol like the White House itself. It's a symbol of our country and the greatness of our country," Trump said.Under the US system, presidents have considerable authority to make changes to the White House, although major construction projects require congressional approval. The president also has the power to designate national monuments, which receive protection and management under federal law.The White House as a whole is already designated a National Historic Landmark. Trump's proclamation acknowledges the existing status but argues that the Oval Office deserves separate recognition and protection as a historically significant space.The office, in its present location, dates back to the early 1930s, when it was established during the presidency of Franklin D Roosevelt.Since beginning his second term, Trump has introduced sweeping decorative changes to the Oval Office, including extensive gold accents, gold-framed paintings and portraits. The president, a former real estate developer, has also pursued several high-profile construction and beautification projects in Washington, DC.However, the move has drawn questions over its significance and whether it can prevent future presidents from making changes.You use AI every day. articles.title: Uber shares one number to tell everyone, how 'unpopular' AI Agents may be on its platform
articles.summary: Tech giants and venture capitalists have spent billions hyping the rise of autonomous personal AI agents.
articles.body: Tech giants and venture capitalists have spent billions hyping the rise of autonomous personal AI agents. They are selling or rather promising a future where software handles everyday tasks like hailing rides and ordering food. But it seems that in the real-world, consumers are still tapping their own screens. During Uber’s third-quarter earnings call, executives disclosed that only four rides worldwide were hailed via an AI agent during the week of Halloween — traditionally regarded as the company’s busiest week of the year.Few hundreds from millionsDeliveries through Uber Eats saw slightly more activity, but the numbers remained negligible. Uber Chief Financial Officer Balaji Krishnamurthy reported that out of roughly 320 million total trips and food delivery orders completed that week, just 500 meals were ordered using an AI intermediary.“It is very, very early and very limited traction that we are seeing so far,” Uber Chief Executive Officer Dara Khosrowshahi told analysts. “Listen, we hope that there will be more traction.”The negligible adoption highlights a stark divide between Silicon Valley’s ambition and everyday consumer behavior. The race to develop agentic AI has ignited massive funding rounds and corporate repositioning across the tech sector. Technology giants such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and SpaceXAI (developer of Grok) have all rolled out task-oriented assistants. Yet public earnings reports reveal that real-world integration remains almost nonexistent. Just last week, delivery rival DoorDash disclosed on its own earnings call that it had recorded only a few hundred AI-initiated orders, noting that users overwhelmingly stick to native apps.Khosrowshahi attributed the muted adoption to simple efficiency. Booking a ride in the standard Uber app takes an average of 50 seconds, he noted, while reordering a favorite meal takes roughly 90 seconds, this actually leaves little friction for an AI agent to solve.Even so, Uber leadership remains optimistic that the technology will eventually expand the company’s footprint. Khosrowshahi noted that roughly eight major assistants currently populate the market, a figure he expects to surpass 10 as adoption matures. “We think that is another opportunity to reach our platform,” Khosrowshahi said. “We think it will be a net positive in terms of demand on the ecosystem.”You use AI every day. articles.title: Nigerian researcher Oghenekevwe William Emadago won $100,000 for making sanitary pads from agricultural waste; his company has already reached 70,000 women and girls
articles.summary: After harvesting bananas, farmers are often left with stems that have little commercial use.
articles.body: After harvesting bananas, farmers are often left with stems that have little commercial use. Oghenekevwe William Emadago, a researcher and entrepreneur from Nigeria, saw an opportunity in this waste. Through his company, Girlified, he is using fibres extracted from banana stems to make sanitary pads. The venture addresses two issues in the country. The difficulty he saw in the early days, some women and girls face in affording menstrual products and the disposal of agricultural waste. In 2026, Emadago received a $100,000 Global Citizen Waislitz People's Choice Award for his work. Girlified has produced millions of pads since its launch in 2021 and aims to reach 10 million women and girls annually by 2030.The childhood experience that led Emadago to develop affordable sanitary padsGlobal Citizen reported that Emadago first became aware of the difficulties surrounding menstrual care while growing up in Northern Nigeria. He saw girls in his community struggle to afford sanitary pads, with some finding it difficult to attend school during their periods. For many families, buying these products every month was an expense they could not easily manage.Years later, the issue became part of his work in research and social entrepreneurship. He began exploring whether materials already available in local communities could help make menstrual products less expensive and easier to access.This eventually led to Girlified, which he co-founded to make sanitary pads from agricultural waste. The venture grew out of two problems he had been looking at: the large amounts of agricultural material left unused after harvesting and the difficulty many women and girls face in accessing affordable menstrual products.How discarded banana stems become part of a sanitary padBanana plants leave behind large quantities of waste after harvesting. Their stems are usually discarded, but the fibres inside them can be put to other uses. Girlified has found a way to use this leftover material in the absorbent core of its sanitary pads.The idea also offers an alternative to the plastic and synthetic materials commonly found in pads. Girlified processes banana stem waste to extract fibres that can be used in its products, giving agricultural leftovers another purpose.Turning the stems into sanitary pads involves more than extracting the fibres. They need to be processed and made suitable for a product that can absorb menstrual fluid. Girlified says its pads are plant-based and plastic-free, with a focus on absorbency and comfort.More than 2.8 million pads produced since 2021Girlified's work has moved beyond the research and product-development stage. According to figures published by Global Citizen and the Waislitz Foundation, the company has produced more than 2.8 million sanitary pads since 2021 and reached over 70,000 women and girls.That reach includes more than the distribution of menstrual products. Girlified says its community programmes also involve menstrual health awareness, educational workshops and sexual health information. The organisation has linked this work with employment opportunities for local women through its manufacturing activities.A $100,000 award brings international recognitionIn August 2026, Emadago was named the winner of the Global Citizen Waislitz People's Choice Award. The recognition was part of the annual Global Citizen Waislitz Awards, presented by Global Citizen and the Waislitz Foundation to individuals developing solutions to social and economic challenges.The 2026 awards included three recipients, each receiving $100,000. Emadago was recognised in the People's Choice category, alongside Smart Israel, who received the Grand Prize, and Diana Yousef, who won the Disruptor Award.The award recognises the work Girlified has already carried out and provides financial support for its next phase of expansion. According to the Waislitz Foundation, the prize money will help the company increase its reach and work towards serving 10 million women and girls every year by 2030.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2018, a man booked flights after finding his train tickets unconfirmed; Railway confirmed them minutes later, leaving him unable to cancel and claim a refund; now, commission awards Rs 19,700 to passenger
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A district consumer commission in Kerala has directed Railway to refund Rs 6,700 to a man whose train tickets were confirmed less than four
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A district consumer commission in Kerala has directed Railway to refund Rs 6,700 to a man whose train tickets were confirmed less than four hours before departure, leaving him no time to cancel them and claim a refund after booking flight tickets. Holding the railway guilty of deficiency in service, the commission said the late confirmation itself deprived him of the opportunity to cancel the tickets within the prescribed deadline.Case backgroundAs per the commission order, Dilip Kumar P S had booked two tickets for his daughter and himself from Hazrat Nizamuddin to Thiruvananthapuram for June 22, 2018. His daughter had received a call letter from the Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) for the post of Assistant Meteorological Officer and was required to appear for document verification at its New Delhi headquarters on that date.For the return journey, they booked tickets through the Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC) on May 24, 2018. Both tickets, one in sleeper class and another in third AC, were waitlisted. The fares were Rs 1,860 and Rs 4,840, respectively. The complainant was monitoring their status daily, hoping to cancel them if they were not confirmed.On June 22, at around 7.20 pm, the complainant and his daughter checked the status at an IRCTC service counter in New Delhi and found that both tickets remained unconfirmed. They then booked flight tickets for their return journey.However, at around 7.39 pm, they received an SMS confirming the railway tickets. They tried to cancel them but, owing to internet connectivity problems, could complete the cancellation only at 8.45pm. Since the train was scheduled to depart at 11.35pm, the tickets could not be cancelled before the four-hour deadline for claiming a refund.The complainant alleged that the railway authorities had informed him about the confirmation only after the refund deadline had effectively passed, causing him financial loss. He approached the commission, alleging deficiency in service and seeking a refund and compensation.In its written statement, Southern Railway argued that passengers could cancel tickets at any time and that confirmation depended on cancellations by other passengers. It said chart preparation was completed four hours before departure and that waitlisted tickets were confirmed according to availability. It also contended that the refund dispute fell within the jurisdiction of the Railway Claims Tribunal.IRCTC argued that it only provided access to the railway reservation system and had no role in preparing charts, confirming berths or deciding refunds. It said the refund decision rested with the concerned railway authorities.Commission's findingsThe bench of president P V Jayarajan and members Preetha G Nair and Viju V R held that Southern Railway's late confirmation of the tickets amounted to deficiency in service. It noted that the confirmation SMS was sent at 7.39pm, less than four hours before the scheduled departure at 11.35pm, leaving the complainant with no opportunity to cancel the tickets within the prescribed period.The commission also rejected Southern Railway's argument that the matter could only be decided by the Railway Claims Tribunal. It said consumer commission proceedings were not barred merely because another legal remedy was available.The bench accepted IRCTC's contention that it had no role in confirming berths or sending confirmation messages, and exonerated it from liability."The intimation of confirmed tickets to the complainant within 4 hours of scheduled departure of train itself restrains the complainant to cancel the confirmed tickets before 4 hours of the scheduled departure of train. The act of the 1st opposite party amounts to deficiency in service, hence 1st opposite party is liable to compensate the complainant," the bench said.Final orderAnnounced on October 27, 2026, the order partly allowed the complaint. The commission directed Southern Railway to pay:Rs 6,700 as refund of the two railway tickets.Rs 10,000 as compensation for mental agony.Rs 3,000 as litigation expenses.The railway must make the payment within one month of receiving the order, failing which the amount, excluding litigation costs, will carry 9 percent annual interest from the date of default until realisation.

articles.title: Trump-Kim reset after midterm blow? Why North Korea may hold the cards
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump could turn his attention to North Korea in search of foreign policy victories after Republicans suffered a major setback in the
articles.body: US President Donald Trump could turn his attention to North Korea in search of foreign policy victories after Republicans suffered a major setback in the midterm elections, but any attempt to revive negotiations with leader Kim Jong Un could put Washington at odds with its closest Asian allies, according to a Reuters report.With the wars in Ukraine and Iran yet to produce diplomatic breakthroughs, analysts and officials in Asia believe Trump may increasingly look towards the region to build his foreign policy legacy during the final two years of his presidency.Kim, with whom Trump has repeatedly expressed an eagerness to restart dialogue, could emerge as a central figure in that effort. However, analysts say Pyongyang has little reason to return to the negotiating table at present, particularly as its military capabilities and strategic partnerships have expanded."Trump is likely to devote significant effort to achieving foreign policy successes, especially if he faces greater constraints on the domestic front," said Ban Kil-joo, an international relations professor at the Korea National Diplomatic Academy in Seoul."Given Trump would want a successor to win in 2028, there is a strong possibility that engagement with North Korea would be part of that agenda," he said.Responding to questions about Trump's plans for diplomacy with Pyongyang, the White House said the president had restored American strength on the global stage and strengthened ties with world leaders."His foreign policy decisions have never been motivated by politics," White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly told Reuters."The commander-in-chief will always act in the best interest of the American people and our national security."Trump met Kim three times during his first presidential term, following an exchange of hostile rhetoric between the two leaders that had raised fears of military confrontation.However, their 2019 summit ended without an agreement after both sides failed to reach a deal on North Korea's nuclear weapons programme and sanctions relief.Seven years later, the negotiating landscape has changed considerably. North Korea has significantly expanded its nuclear and missile arsenal, while its relations with Russia and China have strengthened, leaving Kim with fewer incentives to strike a deal with Washington.That could, in turn, increase pressure on Trump to offer more substantial concessions to bring Pyongyang back to negotiations.Trump calls Kim 'great guy'Trump has repeatedly spoken positively about his relationship with the North Korean leader, describing Kim as a "great guy" and saying the two "get along very well".Despite Trump's interest in restarting engagement, US and South Korean officials see diminishing chances of a meeting this year. Washington has received no response from Pyongyang ahead of a regional summit in China this month, where the two leaders could potentially have met.Kim's influential sister, Kim Yo Jong, has maintained that dialogue remains a possible route to peace but said Pyongyang sees no reason to negotiate at present. She has also criticised what she called Washington's "hostile policy".Her remarks came as she denied US accusations that North Korea had stolen more than $6 billion in virtual assets from Binance last week.Kim Jong Un has previously indicated that he could consider talks if Washington stopped insisting that North Korea abandon its nuclear weapons programme. However, such a shift in US policy would face opposition from regional allies South Korea and Japan."A summit that shelves denuclearisation would undermine deterrence and create policy friction among Washington, Seoul and Tokyo," said Leif-Eric Easley, professor of international studies at Ewha Womans University in Seoul.Officials in Tokyo and Seoul are also concerned that Trump could negotiate directly with Kim, potentially with the tacit approval of Beijing and Moscow, without adequately consulting regional allies, a senior Japanese official told Reuters on condition of anonymity."(Japanese officials) are concerned about the lengths he will go to get a summit with North Korea’s Kim Jong Un, such as dropping the issue of denuclearisation."'Biggest change since World War Two'Trump has referred to North Korea as a nuclear power, although the US and its regional allies have refused to formally recognise that status. Pyongyang is believed to have built dozens of nuclear warheads and accumulated a substantial stockpile of fissile material.Any move by Washington to accept North Korea's nuclear status as part of a diplomatic agreement could fundamentally alter the security landscape in Asia."If US-North Korea talks lead Washington to accept North Korea's nuclear status, the security environment in Asia would change dramatically," said Kazuhiro Maeshima, a professor at Sophia University in Japan."The biggest change since World War Two could occur in the remaining two years of the Trump administration. It is a serious situation."North Korea's military capabilities have also advanced significantly since the 2018-2019 summits. Its arsenal now includes more nuclear weapons and missiles, hypersonic glide vehicles, a growing fleet of modern warships and submarines, and improved drone capabilities.Against this backdrop, bringing Kim back to the negotiating table could require Trump to offer more than limited sanctions relief.However, any major concessions could face resistance from a Democratic-controlled Congress, while Trump's shrinking time in office could further complicate negotiations, said Moon Chung-in, a professor at Yonsei University in Seoul who previously served as a presidential adviser on national security.Moon said Kim would also assess whether Trump had enough political leverage to deliver on any commitments."And what is important is North Korea's perception and calculation; if North Korea thinks that Trump has entered a lame-duck period and he cannot get the support from Congress... there's no reason for Kim Jong Un to come to dialogue," he said.Stephen Biegun, a former US deputy secretary of state who led Washington's negotiations with North Korea during Trump's first term, also sees limited incentives for Pyongyang to engage at present."The North Koreans, I think, have very little upside to a meeting like this right now, and potentially some downside."You use AI every day. articles.title: From ‘habibi’ to ‘hamdulillah’: Abdul El-Sayed’s Senate victory sparks Arab pride
articles.summary: Abdul El-Sayed’s historic election as the first Muslim American to the US Senate has sparked celebrations among Arab communities, with supporters across
articles.body: Abdul El-Sayed’s historic election as the first Muslim American to the US Senate has sparked celebrations among Arab communities, with supporters across the US and the Middle East embracing his use of Arabic expressions such as “habibi” and “inshallah” in American political discourse.El-Sayed, the son of Egyptian immigrants, drew widespread attention with his victory speech, in which he mocked US Vice President JD Vance over his earlier criticism of the Democratic candidate. Addressing Vance, he said, “JD, habibi,” before pointing out that the vice president would be constitutionally required to swear him in when the Senate convenes in January.“Habibi”, which literally means “my beloved”, is commonly used as a term of affection and can also mean “buddy” or “pal” in everyday conversation. The expression became a popular campaign slogan, with supporters wearing T-shirts bearing the words “Habibi for Abdul”.El-Sayed also spoke about how his campaign had turned “inshallah”, meaning “God willing”, into “hamdulillah”, or “thank God”, following his election victory. His use of Arabic expressions resonated with supporters, prompting celebrations and a wave of social media posts featuring Arabic music and cultural references.The celebrations were particularly significant for Arab and Muslim communities, which have faced decades of prejudice and Islamophobic rhetoric in the United States. During the campaign, El-Sayed was subjected to attacks from President Donald Trump and other Republicans. Trump called him a “jihadist” and a “communist”, invoked the September 11 attacks and repeatedly mispronounced his name.Responding to the criticism in his victory speech, El-Sayed said, “Donald, look, I know you've struggled with my name. So after JD swears me in in January, you can just go on and call me ‘senator.'”The 42-year-old epidemiologist, who was born in Michigan to Egyptian immigrant parents, has frequently spoken about his Egyptian heritage, including his family's food and humour and his childhood memories of spending summers in Alexandria, where his father grew up.El-Sayed defeated Republican candidate and former representative Mike Rogers in one of the country's closely watched Senate races. His victory came after he secured the Democratic nomination by defeating Representative Haley Stevens in the party's primary earlier this year.His campaign was centred on progressive policies, including universal healthcare through the Medicare for All proposal and an end to US military aid to Israel. However, he faced a setback in the final days of the campaign when Stevens withdrew her support and endorsed Rogers after attending church with the Republican candidate.Republicans had sought to portray the contest as a referendum on the Democratic Party's progressive wing. Despite the attacks and the withdrawal of Stevens' support, El-Sayed secured the Senate seat, extending the Republican Party's electoral drought in Michigan. Republicans have not won a Senate seat in the state since 1994.El-Sayed will succeed retiring Democratic Senator Gary Peters. His victory was among several electoral breakthroughs for women, candidates of colour and other underrepresented groups in the November 3 midterm elections, in which Democrats also made significant gains in key statewide races and flipped control of both chambers of Congress.You use AI every day. articles.title: Ranjeev Puri makes history as first Indian-American elected Michigan House Speaker
articles.summary: Indian-American lawmaker Ranjeev Puri is set to take charge of the Michigan House of Representatives for the 2027-28 legislative term, becoming the first
articles.body: Indian-American lawmaker Ranjeev Puri is set to take charge of the Michigan House of Representatives for the 2027-28 legislative term, becoming the first person of Indian origin to hold the position.Puri, a Democrat representing Canton, was elected Speaker by his party colleagues on Thursday as Democrats prepared to take control of the 110-member chamber with a 63-47 majority. The party's victory also gives Democrats control of the state's governorship and Senate, creating a Democratic trifecta.Taking to Facebook after the leadership election, the 42-year-old said he was looking forward to working with the incoming state leadership to fulfil campaign promises. “Today, I’m humbled to be elected by my colleagues as Speaker of the Michigan House,” he wrote. “Thank you to my colleagues for your trust. Excited to get to work.”Puri also spoke about the significance of his achievement for his family, whose roots lie in Punjab. “When my parents immigrated to this country, they couldn’t have imagined their son would one day make history, break barriers and lead the Michigan House. That is the promise of America,” he said.In 2020, Puri became the first Sikh American elected to the state House. He was subsequently chosen to lead the Democratic caucus in 2025 in the state, when Republicans held the majority. He is now preparing to enter his fourth term as a state representative.Before his election to the legislature, Puri worked on former US president Barack Obama's presidential campaigns in 2008 and 2012. He later earned an MBA from the University of Chicago Booth School of Business and worked in Michigan's automotive industry.Congratulating him on the elevation, Chintan Patel, executive director of Indian American Impact, said Puri had made reducing household costs, including healthcare and housing expenses, a central part of his work.Patel also said Puri would be expected to stand up for South Asian communities amid rising hate and oppose the Trump administration's policies. “With Ranjeev leading the caucus, we have no doubt they will lower costs and make life more affordable for Michigan families,” he said.Puri's elevation adds to the growing political representation of Indian-Americans following the November 3 midterm elections. Democrats Suhas Subramanyam and Pia Dandiya won seats in the US House, while Ro Khanna and Pramila Jayapal secured re-election. Aruna Miller retained her position as Maryland's lieutenant governor, while Josh Kaul won re-election as Wisconsin attorney general. Indian-American candidates Aparna Raj and Jyot Singh also won races for the Washington DC Council and Georgia state legislature, respectively.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Actor Prakash Raj has urged people to join an anti-Special Intensive Revision (SIR) protest in Kochi on Saturday, November 7, saying citizens
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Actor Prakash Raj has urged people to join an anti-Special Intensive Revision (SIR) protest in Kochi on Saturday, November 7, saying citizens must come together to “save our democracy”.In a video message on X, the actor appealed to students, young people, civil society members and representatives of various organisations to participate in the demonstration against the SIR exercise.“It's very important that we come together and raise our voice to save our democracy,” Raj said, calling on people to join the protest peacefully. Criticising the government and the Election Commission, he added, “We will not tolerate killing democracy.”Titled “Jantar Mantar at Kochi”, the protest will be held at Rajendra Maidan from 4 pm, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) announced in a post on X.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, its south zone lead Vijay Mallangi and national secretary Aafreen Nawaz are expected to attend the event.The Kochi protest comes after CJP members were detained in Delhi while attempting to hold a demonstration against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the SIR exercise.Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das were detained for protesting without permission. Das and Ranka were subsequently arrested after entering the denotified Jantar Mantar site and waving the national flag. They spent a week in jail before being released after giving an undertaking not to organise further protests at the site while it remained denotified.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: No phone, no address: Robbery accused held 40 years after jumping bail in UP
articles.summary: LUCKNOW: Nearly four decades after securing bail from the Allahabad high court and slipping into obscurity, a 65-year-old robbery accused carrying a
articles.body: LUCKNOW: Nearly four decades after securing bail from the Allahabad high court and slipping into obscurity, a 65-year-old robbery accused carrying a reward of Rs 15,000 finally ran out of places to hide. Kanpur Dehat police traced him after a painstaking two-month hunt during which officers posed as village labourers and searched more than 20 possible hideouts.The accused, Balister alias Ramesh Chandra, a native of Muradpur village under Mangalpur police station, was arrested from Auraiya town late Wednesday.According to police, a case under Section 394 of the IPC was registered against him in 1986 for allegedly assaulting a person along with an accomplice and robbing him of Rs 1,500.The accused was initially arrested and spent around one-and-a-half years in jail before securing bail from the Allahabad high court, said Praveen Kumar, SHO, Mangalpur.Kumar said that around 1990, after securing bail, he sold nearly seven bighas of agricultural land and his house in Muradpur and moved to Panipat in Haryana, where he worked in a factory and gradually erased his earlier identity by changing his name to Ramesh Chandra.For years, he left little trail behind, shunning mobile phones, avoiding a permanent address and steering clear of documents that could reveal his identity, according to the SHO.He also married a woman in Panipat and had a son. Following his wife's death in 2002, he sent the child to live with his sister in Muradpur.Kumar said the breakthrough came after police intensified their efforts following the court's intervention and directions to trace the long-absconding accused."With no mobile number or reliable address to track, investigators began questioning relatives and discreetly visiting villages where he was suspected to have connections," the SHO added.The police team spent nearly two months pursuing leads, checking more than 20 possible hideouts and visiting distant relatives. To avoid raising suspicion, personnel even posed as ordinary village labourers, mingling with locals and making discreet inquiries about the fugitive's whereabouts."We visited every household and his over 70 distant relatives to track him," Kumar told TOI.During the investigation, police learnt that the accused occasionally visited relatives but changed locations whenever he sensed police activity. His movements were largely confined to distant family connections, making the search particularly challenging.After tracking his movements through these relatives, the team finally located him at a relative's residence in Auraiya. When police personnel approached him, he reportedly attempted to retreat, but his age made it difficult for him to escape.During questioning, he reportedly disclosed his involvement in several criminal cases, including around 22 robbery cases and two assault cases."We are acting in all cases where accused persons have absconded despite the issuance of non-bailable warrants (NBWs). Police teams have been tasked with tracing and arresting such fugitives, and efforts are underway to ensure their apprehension," said Shraddha Narendra Pandey, SP, Kanpur Dehat.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Lucknow | Silver Rate in Lucknow | Bank Holidays in Lucknow | Public Holidays in Lucknow | Lucknow AQI | Weather in Lucknow | Petrol Price in Lucknow | Diesel Price in Lucknow | CNG Price in Lucknow | LPG Price in LucknowStay updated with the latest Lucknow news. articles.title: The Swiftie travel guide through Taylor Swift’s song lyrics: From New York to London, Paris to Florida and beyond
articles.summary: Imagine you’re planning your next trip not from Pinterest or a travel brochure, but straight from your favorite Taylor Swift songs.
articles.body: Imagine you’re planning your next trip not from Pinterest or a travel brochure, but straight from your favorite Taylor Swift songs. Suddenly, you’re wandering New York with ‘1989’ blasting in your headphones, or you’re strolling through London’s Camden Market because ‘London Boy’ tells you it’s the place to be. For die-hard Swift fans, her albums turn every city, street, and landscape into a scrapbook: a memory packed with relationships, heartache, daydreams, and adventure.The intriguing part is, she doesn’t just name-drop locations for fun. Taylor turns real places into emotional mile-markers. Sometimes, the city’s the stage for a whirlwind romance. In other moments, a nook or a pub becomes the backdrop for heartbreak or nostalgia. Whether it’s New York’s energy, Florida’s beaches, the English Lake District’s tranquil beauty, or the heart of Nashville, her lyrics are basically a global itinerary.Most amazing of all? These spots aren’t fantasy; they’re real, and you can actually visit them. If you’re looking to make your next adventure a little more magical or just want to trace the ‘Taylor Swift map’, here’s a global tour with her lyrics as your guide.New York: Where ‘Welcome to New York’ comes to lifeStart in Greenwich Village, on Cornelia Street, which inspired Taylor’s song of the same name. It’s become an emotional landmark: it’s where she rented a townhouse here, baked memories into lyrics, and fans now flock to snap photos at No. 23. Next, head to Central Park’s rowboats, channeling some of that romantic vibe from ‘The Bolter’. Looking for a classic slice of NYC nostalgia? Coney Island, with its vibrant boardwalk, old-school amusement park, and the iconic Wonder Wheel, sets the scene for the bittersweet song ‘Coney Island.’ And if you’re the literary sort, check out Hotel Chelsea, as Taylor gives it a nod in ‘The Tortured Poets Department.’ The hotel isn’t just fancy; it’s soaked in writer and musician history.London: Taylor’s songbook tourTaylor’s relationship with London is full of detail. ‘London Boy’ pretty much doubles as a map. Begin at Camden Market, where the city’s alternative vibe flourishes. Wander through Highgate, Brixton, Shoreditch, and Hackney — each of those neighborhood spots gets its moment in her lyrics, each offering its own flavor. Hampstead Heath shows up in both ‘London Boy’ and ‘So Long, London’: same place, totally different mood. Want to be part of the fan pilgrimage? ‘The Black Dog’ pub in Vauxhall has become a Swiftie hotspot thanks to her new album. Nobody really knows if it’s the official inspiration, but fans don’t mind.Paris: Romance, daydreams, and ‘Midnights’Paris is tailor-made for a Swift-inspired break. Her song ‘Paris’ from ‘Midnights’ is all about being caught up in love, tuning out the rest of the world. The city, with its winding streets, café terraces, and iconic sights like the Eiffel Tower, Montmartre, and the Seine, pairs perfectly as a playlist backdrop. And lately, Swift’s ‘Elizabeth Taylor’ on her 2025 album even references the Hotel Plaza Athénée, adding a layer of old Hollywood glamour to her Paris lore.Destin, Florida: Escape to Swift’s ‘Florida!!!’One can’t deny, sometimes you just need sand, sunshine, and a reset. Taylor’s ‘Florida!!!’ (featuring Florence + The Machine) gives Destin its moment. The beaches are white, the water’s blue-green, and places like Henderson Beach State Park and Crab Island offer a true getaway. It’s the ultimate soundtrack for starting again and leaving your worries behind.Rhode Island: The ‘Last Great American Dynasty’Taylor’s song about Rebekah Harkness and Holiday House reveals a real location: it’s her mansion in Watch Hill, Rhode Island. While you can’t tour Holiday House itself (it’s private), you can visit Watch Hill. The little village has a nostalgic charm, and Watch Hill Beach or the historic Flying Horse Carousel are worth seeing. Nearby, Misquamicut State Beach makes for some classic Rhode Island seaside chill.The Lake District, England: Where ‘The Lakes’ beckonsIf you love the poetic vibe of ‘folklore’ and ‘evermore,’ the Lake District checks all the boxes. Taylor’s lyrics in ‘The Lakes’ paint Windermere and its surroundings as wild, beautiful, and moody, which is ideal for slowing down and getting lost in thought. Ambleside, Grasmere, and the whole region invite you to unplug, stroll, and imagine you’re living inside a Taylor Swift song.Nashville and Georgia: Where the story beganNashville is the beating heart of Taylor’s early career. Songs like ‘Invisible String’ call out places like Centennial Park (with its replica Parthenon), while ‘I Think He Knows’ takes you to the famous Music Row on 16th Avenue. And don’t forget Georgia, as her song ‘Tim McGraw’ references its starry sky, holding onto teenage nostalgia. These spots give Taylor’s fans a window into the country roots that made her a superstar.A global tour and a Taylor Swift song at every stopIf you chart your journey based on Taylor’s lyrics, you won’t just see places; you’ll step into chapters of life, moments of heartbreak, and flashes of joy. New York brings excitement and possibility; London mixes romance and melancholy; Paris is pure fantasy; the Lake District whispers solitude and inspiration.Taylor Swift’s magic is turning ordinary streets and beaches into personal landmarks. For Swifties or anyone who loves music with their travel, maybe it’s time to leave the guidebooks behind. Build your next trip from her songbook, and let each destination become a new memory: one lyric, one adventure at a time.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: A veteran Arab lawmaker in Israel is willing to break with precedent to topple Netanyahu
articles.summary: Veteran Arab politician Ahmad Tibi expresses willingness to ally with Jewish-led parties to overthrow Prime Minister Netanyahu, breaking with historical precedent. Tibi's approach highlights complexities in Israeli politics and potential impacts on Palestinian citizens' lives.
articles.body: TAYIBE: A veteran Arab lawmaker in Israel says his bloc is willing to break with decades of precedent and join forces with Jewish-led parties in a shared bid to end Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's long rule."We want to do things that we did not do in the past in order to remove this criminal government," Ahmad Tibi, a senior member of the Arab Joint List, told the Associated Press.But any such partnership could be politically fraught for both sides. For the Joint List, it would mean backing a government unlikely to end Israel's wars or curb settlement expansion in the occupied West Bank. For Netanyahu's opponents, it would mean aligning with parties that not only criticize Israel's policies, but reject its identity as a Jewish state.After historic voter turnout delivered Arab-led parties a record share in Israel's parliament, Tibi said the Joint List is willing to support an anti-Netanyahu government without joining it. That could reassure Jewish-led factions that view them with suspicion and satisfy their own constituents. It would still give the Joint List major influence.Only one Arab party has ever served in an Israeli government, in 2021. But that party, Ra'am, is much more conciliatory than the Joint List and held fewer seats. Ra'am is willing to join another anti-Netanyahu government as a partner, but any such arrangement would still need the support of the Joint List.If the Jewish-led parties reject such a partnership, then it would prove Israel is "an ethnocracy, not an absolute democracy for all citizens," Tibi said.The Joint List's positions put it at odds with most IsraelisMost of the Palestinian population in what is now Israel fled or was expelled during the 1948 war surrounding its creation. Those who remained were granted citizenship, including the right to vote, and today they and their descendants make up some 20% of the population.Many Jewish Israelis have historically viewed Arab-led political parties with suspicion. That distrust has been reinforced by lawmakers who have defended or praised Israel's enemies.The Joint List, a coalition of three left-wing and nationalist parties, rejects what it refers to as the "racist Zionist consensus" in Israel. It calls for partnering with Jewish Israelis who support a Palestinian state in the West Bank, Gaza and east Jerusalem, territories occupied in the 1967 Mideast war. It rejects Israel's identity as a Jewish state, calling for equal rights for all its citizens.Many Jewish Israelis see that as support for the country's enemies at a time of war. Netanyahu has encouraged such sentiments, lodging unproven accusations of electoral fraud against the Arab-led parties and portraying them as a threat to national security.A dilemma for Netanyahu's opponentsThat creates a dilemma for Netanyahu's main opponents, led by former general Gadi Eisenkot.In the campaign, they portrayed Netanyahu as a corrupt leader who failed to prevent the October 7, 2023, attack and then blocked a public inquiry into it. They cast the election in existential terms, saying Netanyahu's far-right government threatened Israel's democratic institutions.They won 48 seats in the 120-member Knesset, compared to 53 for Netanyahu's coalition. The Joint List won 11 seats and Ra'am won 8, making them crucial to forming an anti-Netanyahu majority.The Joint List could help an anti-Netanyahu bloc take power by voting for it or by abstaining to lower the threshold needed for a majority. Either arrangement could allow opposition parties to form a government without requiring the Joint List to become part of their administration. Joining could put its lawmakers in the uncomfortable position of being part of a government waging wars in Gaza and Lebanon that they oppose.Some of Eisenkot's allies welcome Arab support while others are opposed, pointing to past statements by Joint List leaders they argue deny Israel's legitimacy or support its enemies.Tibi said he was under no illusions that a partnership with Netanyahu's opponents would end the wars or bring about a Palestinian state. But he said a "repair government" would improve the lives of Palestinian citizens, by ending Netanyahu's rule and also potentially addressing local issues like a wave of violent crime in Arab communities.It's unclear what conditions would be requiredEisenkot has said Arab-led parties must meet certain conditions in any partnership, including calling Hamas a terrorist group that needs to be destroyed.Tibi said the conditions do not apply to parties like the Joint List that want to provide outside support.The Joint List and Ra'am have denounced the Hamas-led Oct. 7 attack and any violence against civilians. But they have refused to brand Hamas a terrorist group or call for its destruction, saying that doing so would justify Israel's devastating military campaign in Gaza.Tibi said both the October 7 attack and Israel's response to it were immoral.The veteran lawmaker has long been a lightning rod for right-wing attacks on Arab parties. During Israel's 2019 elections, Netanyahu, popularly known as Bibi, campaigned on the slogan "Bibi or Tibi?" to warn voters that opposing him meant relying on Arab-led parties to form a government.Tibi said Tuesday that the election result had turned the slogan on its head."When he said 'Bibi or Tibi,' he incited against Arabs," he said. "Now, it's 'Tibi,' because Arab voters went in a very massive way to take part in the elections. It's definitely our story this time."You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: North Dakota ranchers fought a gas company's pipeline easement and won $383,375 in legal costs, only to lose the award on appeal; their dispute is now headed to the US Supreme Court on November 9
articles.summary: The US Supreme Court will hear a dispute on Monday over whether a private natural gas pipeline company must pay the legal expenses of landowners whose
articles.body: The US Supreme Court will hear a dispute on Monday over whether a private natural gas pipeline company must pay the legal expenses of landowners whose property it acquires through eminent domain.The case involves North Dakota rancher Leonard Hoffmann and his neighbours, who won an award of $383,375.76 in attorney's fees and litigation expenses against WBI Energy Transmission, according to SCOTUS Analytics. However, the US Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit overturned the award in March 2025, ruling that federal law, rather than state law, governs compensation in such cases. The ranchers have now challenged that decision before the Supreme Court.The dispute began in 2018 when WBI Energy Transmission informed Hoffmann and other landowners in North Dakota that it planned to acquire an easement across their ranchland for a natural gas pipeline. An easement gives another party the right to use a specific portion of privately owned property. Although WBI is a private company, it holds a federal certificate that allows it to exercise eminent domain powers under the Natural Gas Act.According to the Institute for Justice, the public-interest law firm representing the ranchers, WBI initially offered them about half the property's market value. The landowners challenged the proposed amount and took the dispute to court.The parties eventually reached a settlement over the value of the property. However, they left unresolved whether the company was also required to pay the landowners' legal fees and other expenses incurred during the proceedings.
